input.question: how do we know that the emails released from Wikileaks are real and not at all fabricated or edited?
input.ground_truth: I think the best metric we have is how the people involved in said emails respond. Seeing as how Debbie Wasserman-Schultz resigned over them, as well as another higher up in the democratic party did recently (I believe) it means they were most likely real. If the people involved were protesting their legitimacy that may be a sign they were fabricated. That being said, no one can say for sure except the people in the emails in question I suppose.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you get a letter from a friend. How do you know it’s really from your friend and not someone pretending to be them?

For the emails from Wikileaks, smart people called “experts” check them in special ways. They look for clues, like a secret code (called a “digital signature”) that the real sender puts on the email, just like you might draw a little heart at the end of a note to show it’s from you.

Also, sometimes lots of other people saw the emails before Wikileaks shared them, or the emails talk about things that really happened. So, if the emails match what everyone else saw or what really happened, we can be pretty sure they are real.

But, sometimes it’s still tricky, and people have to keep checking and asking questions to be sure!
